👥 Who Is Obligated to Light — deaf-mutes, minors, women, and a lodging guest
🙏 Who Blesses, and How Many Blessings, Night by Night
⚖️ The Priority Ladder — Shabbat lamp, Chanukah lamp, and kiddush wine
🌟 Reward for Diligence — Rav Huna's and Rav Chisda's predictions from candlelight

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Obligation, Blessing, and Priority
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 23a–23b
overview.hebrewSource: אָסוּר לְהַרְצוֹת מָעוֹת כְּנֶגֶד נֵר חֲנוּכָּה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens with proof that lighting, not placement, accomplishes the Chanukah mitzva — settled from the practice of extinguishing and relighting a lantern that burned all Shabbat, and from the wording of the blessing itself. From there the Gemara maps who is obligated: not a deaf-mute, imbecile, or minor, but certainly a woman, since 'they too were included in the miracle,' and even a guest lodging with a host. It works out the blessing formula and how many blessings are said on the first night versus later nights, establishes a strict order of priority when a poor person can afford only one lamp, and closes with a cluster of teachings on the reward for lighting generously — plus the correct timing, neither too early nor too late.

slides.title: 🔦 Proof: Lighting Accomplishes the Mitzva
slides.subtitle: A lantern already burning, and the wording of the blessing itself

nodes.content: 🏮 Case: a lantern burns through all of Shabbat; at Shabbat's end, one extinguishes it and relights it as the Chanukah light
❓ If placing accomplishes the mitzva, the halakha should read 'extinguish, lift it, set it down, and light' — but it doesn't say that
🙏 Further proof: the blessing recited is '…to light the Chanukah lamp' — over the act of lighting itself
✅ Conclusion: hadlaka oseh mitzva — lighting, not placement, accomplishes the mitzva

callout.label: Immediate consequence:
callout.text: If a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor lights the lamp, nothing has been accomplished — even if a competent adult later moves it into place. A woman, however, is certainly fit to light, since she too was saved in the miracle.

slides.title: 👥 Who Must Light — and Who Is Exempt
slides.subtitle: From incapacity to hospitality
rows: Lack the intellectual capacity required for a valid mitzva-act
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: women were included in the very miracle being commemorated
Fulfilled through the host's lighting, or by contributing coins as a partner
Contributed coins before marriage; relied on his home's lighting after
As a bachelor he partnered with his host; once married, his wife's lighting covered him

slides.title: 🙏 The Blessing Formula, Night by Night
slides.subtitle: Three sages weigh in on who blesses and how many blessings

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav (via Rav Chiyya bar Ashi): one who lights must recite a blessing
2️⃣ Rabbi Yirmeya: one who merely sees a burning Chanukah light must also bless
3️⃣ Rav Yehuda's formula, night one: the one who lights says three blessings; the one who only sees says two

4️⃣ From night two onward: the lighter says two, the seer says one — the blessing dropped is shehecheyanu ('who has given us life'), since it applies only to the first time each year, while the miracle blessing applies every night

callout.label: Where is the command?
callout.text: Since Chanukah isn't in the Torah, the blessing 'who commanded us' is grounded homiletically: Rav Avya derives it from 'you shall not turn aside' (Deut. 17:11), the general obligation to heed the Sages.

slides.title: ⚖️ When Oil Money Is Scarce: What Comes First
slides.subtitle: Rava's ranked priorities for a poor household

boxes.title: Shabbat Home Lamp Wins
items: Home lamp beats Chanukah lamp — because of shalom bayit, peace in the home
Home lamp beats kiddush wine — same reason: a family shouldn't eat in darkness

boxes.title: Chanukah Lamp vs. Kiddush
items: Rava's dilemma: does kiddush win because it's frequent (tadir), or Chanukah win for publicizing the miracle?
Rava resolves it himself: Chanukah wins — pirsumei nisa, publicizing the miracle, takes precedence

callout.label: Also on this daf:
callout.text: A courtyard with two entrances facing different directions needs a lamp at each, to avoid the suspicion of passersby who see only one door lit — echoing the four reasons the Torah requires pe'a specifically at the end of a field.

slides.title: 🌟 Diligence in Small Mitzvot, Rewarded in Children
slides.text: Rav Huna teaches that one accustomed to kindling lights merits children who are Torah scholars. Passing the home of Rabbi Avin the carpenter and seeing him light many lamps, Rav Huna predicted: 'Two great men will emerge from here' — and indeed Rav Idi bar Avin and Rav Chiyya bar Avin did. Rav Chisda made the same prediction about Rav Sheizvi's family. But timing still matters: when Rav Yosef's wife lit too early, an Elder corrected her from the verse about the pillars of cloud and fire — light neither too early nor too late.
slides.hebrewSource: הָרָגִיל בְּנֵר הָוְיִין לֵיהּ בָּנִים תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים

summary.principle: Because lighting itself accomplishes the Chanukah mitzva, the Gemara can precisely define who must perform that act, how many blessings accompany it, and — when resources are scarce — which lamp takes priority, always favoring domestic peace first and publicizing the miracle second.

flowSteps.content: 🔦 The lantern case and the blessing's own wording prove: lighting, not placing, accomplishes the mitzva
👥 Deaf-mutes, imbeciles, and minors cannot fulfill it; women are obligated; a guest is covered by his host

columns.content: 🙏 First night: 3 blessings for the lighter, 2 for the viewer; fewer thereafter
⚖️ Home lamp beats Chanukah lamp and kiddush; Chanukah beats kiddush

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: shalom bayit governs the home lamp's priority, and pirsumei nisa — publicizing the miracle — governs the Chanukah lamp's priority over kiddush

quiz.q: What proof does the Gemara bring that lighting, rather than placing, accomplishes the Chanukah mitzva?
o: A verse in the Torah explicitly states it
The practice of extinguishing and relighting a lantern at Shabbat's end, and the wording of the blessing itself, both point to lighting
The testimony of the Hasmonean priests
Rabban Gamliel's ruling about the sons
quiz.e: Since one only extinguishes and relights the lantern (rather than also moving it), and the blessing text refers to the act of lighting, the Gemara concludes that hadlaka — lighting — accomplishes the mitzva.

quiz.q: Why are women obligated in lighting the Chanukah lamp, according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?
o: Because women are generally exempt from time-bound positive mitzvot, but this one was singled out
Because women too were included in the miracle that Chanukah commemorates
Because women light the Shabbat lamp, so the same applies to Chanukah
Because a special decree was issued for women only
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi teaches that women are obligated because 'they too were included in that miracle' (af hein hayu be'oto hanes).

quiz.q: According to Rav Yehuda's formula, how many blessings does one who lights the Chanukah lamp recite on the first night, and which blessing is dropped afterward?
o: Two blessings on the first night; the miracle blessing is dropped afterward
Three blessings on the first night; the shehecheyanu blessing is dropped on later nights
One blessing every night, no changes
Four blessings on the first night, decreasing by one each night
quiz.e: On the first night the lighter recites three blessings (including shehecheyanu); from the second night on, only two, since shehecheyanu applies only to the first performance of the mitzva each year, while the miracle blessing applies throughout.

quiz.q: According to Rava, when a poor household must choose between a Chanukah lamp and wine for Shabbat-day kiddush, which takes priority and why?
o: Kiddush, because it is a more frequent obligation
The Chanukah lamp, because of pirsumei nisa — publicizing the miracle
Neither; both are equally deferred to buy food instead
The home lamp always wins over both
quiz.e: After raising the dilemma between the frequent (tadir) principle favoring kiddush and the value of publicizing the miracle, Rava resolves that the Chanukah lamp takes precedence due to pirsumei nisa.

quiz.q: What did Rav Huna predict upon seeing Rabbi Avin the carpenter light many lamps in his home, and what happened?
o: That his house would burn down; it did not
That two great scholars would emerge from that house, and indeed Rav Idi bar Avin and Rav Chiyya bar Avin did
That he would become wealthy from selling oil
Nothing — Rav Huna made no such prediction
quiz.e: Rav Huna, noting the household's diligence in lighting, said 'two great men will emerge from here,' and the Gemara records that Rav Idi bar Avin and Rav Chiyya bar Avin indeed came from that family.
